name: Highlands 28

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, where a paved road runs along the bottom of the frame with a paved driveway spur intersecting it and leading into the densely vegetated lot|The residence is fully screened from the front street by a dense cluster of mature conifer trees, eliminating direct visual contact with the structure from the frontage|The approach from the street into the property is a single-lane paved driveway that curves through the tree cover before reaching the residence.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property, which is characterized by dense stands of mature conifers across sandy, scrubby terrain with no visible fencing or gates on this side|A paved road is visible along the right edge of the frame, running parallel to the property boundary|No secondary structures, outbuildings, or access routes are visible on the right side through the tree cover.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which consists of open sandy terrain transitioning to a densely wooded interior with no visible structures, outbuildings, fencing, or access routes from this direction|The terrain across the rear of the property is relatively open at the outer perimeter with increasing vegetation density toward the residence|No rear driveway or path connecting to the rear boundary is visible.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, where a paved driveway is visible running along the left edge of the frame and leading into the lot from the street|The property on this side features open sandy ground transitioning to dense conifer vegetation that screens the residence from view|No fencing, gates, or secondary structures are visible on the left side.

considerations: The residence is set well back from the street and is heavily screened on all sides by dense mature conifer trees, significantly limiting sightlines and visibility of the structure from any perimeter approach. Access to the property is via a single paved driveway entering from the front street, with no observable secondary or rear access routes. The dense conifer canopy throughout the lot creates a continuous vegetation barrier that could impede ground movement and increase navigation difficulty for responders attempting to reach or circle the structure. Staging area is limited to the driveway approach and immediate street frontage.
clarifications: Does the driveway provide sufficient width and vertical clearance through the tree canopy for full-size emergency apparatus? Is there a turnaround area at or near the residence sufficient to accommodate a fire engine or ambulance? Are there any locked gates or access controls on the driveway between the street and the residence? Are there any additional structures, propane tanks, or fuel storage on the property not visible through the tree canopy?
